summary: We built Skypatch, a web tool that lets anyone view NASA SPHEREx data for a chosen area of the sky. The user enters a sky position, a cutout size and a detector, and gets an image in the browser. Skypatch searches the NASA/IPAC IRSA archive and requests only a small cutout, not the full FITS file of about 70 MB. It converts the cutout to a PNG and labels it with its wavelength. A sidebar adds tools such as observation dates, object spectrum, Gaia matches, motion maps, defect masks and contrast controls. We used Next.js, FastAPI, Astropy and Supabase. Skypatch makes SPHEREx data easy to open for students and researchers, with no special software and no FITS knowledge.
details:
What Skypatch does

Skypatch displays NASA SPHEREx data in the specified area. The user enters a position, a cutout size, and a detector, and receives an image following these parameters. The best thing is that no special software or FITS knowledge is required.

How it works

The user enters a sky position (RA and Dec), a cutout size, and a detector. Skypatch searches the NASA/IPAC IRSA archive for every SPHEREx image that covers the user's spot request. Full FITS files weigh about 70 MB each, so Skypatch never downloads them. Instead, it uses the IRSA cutout service to receive only the small patch that covers the target and converts it to a standard PNG, which is then shown in the browser.  Each image carries its wavelength at their position, because SPHEREx wavelength changes across the detector.

Why it helps 

SPHEREx data sits in large FITS files with multiple extensions. Most people can’t open them. Students explore real NASA data in minutes. Researchers skip the slow download when they need only a small area. Small cutouts and light PNGs also transfer faster.

Tools

  • Next.js (React) for the frontend, Figma for design
  • Vercel (frontend), Render (backend), Supabase (PostgreSQL database)
  • FastAPI, Uvicorn — API backend; Pydantic, pydantic-settings — validation and configuration; NumPy - numerical processing; Astropy - astronomical data processing; Reproject - image alignment; HTTPX - API requests; Astroquery, PyVO - archive access; Pillow, Matplotlib - visualization; Supabase - database and storage; Docker — deployment; pytest - testing.

GitHub: https://github.com/bapeyms/SkySurveySPHEREx.git
